"VRChat login method overly sensitive to IP address changes"

"VRChat login method incompatible with cgnat"

Just thinking of a better title for practice and also maybe for when you resubmit in future.

Using the term cgnat might be useful. 

Personally I use steam and meta login method. Don't get hassled with codes. Maybe that's how VRChat themselves haven't noticed? I think with mobile client you can link a Google account as well.

I'm not sure if VRChat encourages people to link accounts. I do know they encourage VRChat accounts themselves as it's required to upload content.

@{62df7cd83e007e467295c4e1|full_name}

Hi, thanks for your kindly advice, and sorry for that since I'm not a native English speaker, and I'm not good at it. Sorry for any mistake, confused and misleading. 

> Using the term cgnat might be useful. 

CGNAT is just one of the many reasons, and probably the least one. May you didn't get the "country" reason based on what you said, so let me explain it clearly. 

The 2nd reason is probably the biggest one for us, since connecting to VRChat server directly is not a great experience, because your connection to VRChat or EAC (and any other online games operated in worldwide) may be fked up randomly. If anyone fk up, everything fk up. 

To get the most stable network, we usually use a software called "game/network accelerator", which is just a proxy software. By using such software, your network packets related to the game will go through their high quality, high priority, low latency business-tier network, and bypass many unstable "factors". So in a short, the software is a "must have" for many players. 

However, since you're choosing one of thousands landing servers, your IP address (or even country/region) to the game will be various based on the target server. Besides, the software usually choose the lowest latency one by default, which is different every time when you start the game. So that's the reason why remove thr IP restriction is important to us (and related multiple IPs login leads to possible ban). 

> Personally I use steam and meta login method. Don't get hassled with codes. 

If you're in NA, I guess your IP is sticked so that you don't have such issue, since the IPv4 pools assigned to USA is very large. I've heard rumors that even your phone can be assigned a static IP when using university hotspot. So unless you asked your ISP, your IP will probably never change. Though all of these are just my imagination, and I haven't check if it works since I don't link any accounts. 

> Maybe that's how VRChat themselves haven't noticed? 

They knew it, and that's why I said they didn't fix it after 4 years since they got conclusion. 

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/allow-authcookie-to-be-used-from-a-different-ip-address-extra-features

As EAC is already implemented, I don't think they have any other excuse.

> I think with mobile client you can link a Google account as well. 

Google Services is not available for most Chinese phones. That's why I said you didn't get it. 🤣 

> I'm not sure if VRChat encourages people to link accounts. 

I think it's just for backport, or just let new user get interests without registering account.
@{6635cd6bef5ac79a229017ea|full_name} I mentioned the linked accounts, when I log in with VRChat directly I get hassled every week. Logging in via META account, I don't get hassled.

@{62df7cd83e007e467295c4e1|full_name} That sounds nice, thanks for the information!

Though I think the issue about offical account login still needs to be fixed, since not every user wants to (or can) link their account. Like linking Steam is not a big issue, but linking Meta account is probably as hard as linking Google account (I'm not sure if VRChat can link Pico CN account, because it's not the same system as International version, and VRC is not published in CN store). 

So for now, let's just see how will staff answer the IP issue.

Since there's a numerous of people getting falsy banned in my region when using said software yesterday, and it seems like it's because of the IP issue. 

https://x.com/VRChat/status/1814738416648790267

https://x.com/VRChat/status/1814737968315441268

Though the staff has already reverted the ban, please sincerely consider moving the authorized logic to hardware based.

IP based security check & login detect is not that suitable for today, people may changes their IP for many reasons, not only for privacy, but also a-must-have probably (I've heard some of the VRChat features like SDK upload has been blocked in my region last month, so the only way and stable way to access VRC is using such software). Again, I don't see any other games using EAC has such strict limits.

When using such software, it'll choose the lowest latency server to connect for best game latency. However the server may be randomize because of the network load. Besides, it's only related to what server we can connect, the outbounding traffic is not controllable, since it'll choose the closest server to the game server, too.

By switching to HWID based, if the ID is not changed, then you can say the session is trusted, and no need to check its IP (or you can just send an E-mail to say the user is logged in in other country), which should resolve such issue.

Again, you can always ask user to trust this device or not, so that the user can choose to use HWID based session or current IP based session.

An example of IP is changed too often because of the outbounding IP changes.

https://x.com/miaozesang233/status/1814956253657059576

SDK side is probably hard to implement HWID (though SDK upload is still an issue here, because it's being completely blocked since last month. I suspect VCC should have a similar situation here. The only way is to use proxy / VPN / said software with route mode to upload assets, not sure if it's free now).

But at least, you can only limit it to the clients that have a reliable hardware fingerprint, like PC client (I guess EAC should have a SDK API to get HWID, and since it's provided by EAC, it's safe unless you don't trust EAC), Android without ROOT (Android ID or just write a random UUID in /data/data/ since no one can access it except root) or iPhone.

details:
I'm not sure should it be "Feature Requests" or "Bug Reports", but since it's producable, it's not related to setup, and of course it has an expected result, so I report it here.

## What happened?

When the outbound IP of your device is changed, you'll be forced to logout, and have to type your username and password again, wait for OTP email and type again. If that's not annoying, thinking if you're in VR and you have to put off and put on your headset again and again.

## Why it's required?

1. IP change is very common based on your ISP. If your ISP gives you a static, never changed IP, then you're good to go. However, some ISP may change your IP by day, for that case, you're in the login hell. For example, due to shortage of IPv4 addresses, most of users in my country are behind NAT, so your outbound IP may be vary based on ISP's routers. If you acquire a public IP to attach to your network, your IP is still going to change in around 3 days, which is your DHCP or PPPoe lease time. Static IP is not an option since it's tight to business, and it's too expensive for endpoint user.

2. Because of the uncontrollable unstable network reasons (if you just to know which "country" I mean in previous section), some of the users may use a special software to play their games. Technically, it's more like a VPN or proxy software, which only routes your playing game process and related services (like Steam network and Easy Anti-cheat) to their high-priority stable business network, then landing to their datacenter which closest to the game servers, so that you can get the least ping delay and least package loss (of course, it's business-tier network). It's a very common situation in my country, and for now I don't see any games or anti-cheats (like EAC or BattlEye) are unhappy with that, except VRChat, due to the previous IP change problem, since your IP may vary based on their best selected server, which changed by time based on network traffic.

3. You're playing VRChat on your Android phone? That's very nice! Now go to somewhere where Wi-Fi signal is weak. At the time you entered your bathroom, your Wi-Fi is disconnected, your phone is using cellular data, you have been kicked out from VRChat, you have to kill VRChat because it just shows the loading logo again and again (you're in the Unity player, not webview, so no login webview pop-up), you have to launch VRChat, you have to type your username and password again, you have to switch to your 2FA / email app to see the code, and switch back to the game, just to see your instance is revoked. All of these is because your IP is changed! You're tired, you get off the bathroom. Congratulation! Your phone is connected to Wi-Fi! Your outbound IP is changed back! You have to do it again!

## How to fix that?

Please give an option to remember the user on the device. Please.

## Ho to fix that... technically?

Switch the login token to hardware-id based or unique-id based, instead of IP based.

In case of breaking change to old clients, if user enabled "Remember me / Trust this device" in new client, add a new field to the login API, and fill it with the new hwid/uuid token. New client save the new token, and old client / new client without "Remember me" use the previous token.

If adding a new field is not an option, because the client requires a specific format of response data, then just return the hwid/uuid based token to the old field. On server side, a simple try catch will do the trick.

If hwid can only be get from client, then only implement it to VRChat client. You don't have to apply it to website / SDK, fixing your client is enough. Putting your headset off and on is really annoying.

## Is that safe for user?

Of course, I don't see any games or software are having the issue, except VRChat. The only one I see which is a bit strict is Parsec (fun fact, it is a subsidiary company of Unity now), since it's a kind of remote control software. However, it only validates your IP on login. If you've logged in before, unless your credential is expired, you're still logged-in no matter what IP you're using and whether it changed. I can't see any situation that VRChat is required to be more secure than a remote control software.

If you still think it's dangerous, just send a regular warning email to the user's email address when the IP is changed. Come on, you've already sent an email (OTP) to the user, just replace it with warning email, with the login IP and located country / region / state attached. If the user doesn't change his login area, just changes his IP, then you don't need to pay for another email, profit.

Since the user manually tick the "Trust this device" option, you can say the user has already accept any possible risk.

## The bug is already reported

So you mean you didn't fix it after nearly 5 years?

And even after noting the conclusion 4 years?

Besides, it's now affected to new Android user, and as I said, it's more common than regular PC user, like I received ~5 OTC email and finally gave up login. And I've heard that VRChat may reject user login if a user changes his IP too often, then switching from Wi-Fi to 5G/4G/whateverG back and forth may resulting the IP ban.

I don't check if it also happens to Quest / Pico device, but since it's a server-side logic, I think they're also affected, so I selected them, too.

* 0505 update: Tested on a Pico device, and can confirm it's also affected.

## What if someone steal the login token and simulate the same hwid?

Is that mean EAC is 💩?
